title: Stratum pullback and scalar-extension comparison
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings, and let $i:S\to T$ be an immersion identifying $S$ with a locally closed constructible stratum as in [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], constant ring and module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf], and module inverse image $i^*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For a finite $A$-module $M$, inverse image identifies $i^*\underline M_T\simeq\underline M_S$ as $A_S$-modules, compatibly with addition, negation, zero and scalar multiplication; the coefficient comparison identifies $i^{-1}A_T$ with $A_S$. If $P$ is a K-flat complex [def-pc-kflat-complex] of $A_T$-modules with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], then $i^*P$ is K-flat with flat terms and there is a natural termwise tensor comparison [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]
$$i^*(P\otimes_{A_T}B_T)\simeq i^*P\otimes_{A_S}B_S.$$
If the cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] of a complex $K$ restrict to finite locally constant $A_S$-modules on $S$, exact coefficient pullback identifies $\mathcal H^q(i^*K)$ with $i^*\mathcal H^q(K)$ for every $q$.

proof.text: Use the canonical coefficient comparison for invertibility. Compose the constant-module presheaf/evaluation adjunction with simultaneous module sheafification. Base change preserves the final object. Identity on sections identifies the two global-section functors; linearity follows from the constant-section coefficient equation. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives the constant-module isomorphism. Its unit equation at the terminal object and naturality along the map to that object give the displayed formula at every object.

Construct scalar extension as a functor using the existing sectionwise tensor maps and sheafification. Its tensor-unit Hom equivalence is the normalized change-of-rings adjunction. The existing coefficient direct-image comparison is identity on sections; bridge its pushforward to the arbitrary-ring pushforward by the adjunction triangle identity. Uniqueness of the two composite left adjoints gives beta, its naturality, and its tensor-unit equation. Apply naturality to each differential and use HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents to assemble the complex comparisons.

Use the algebraic presentation of the specified inverse-image module functor and finite-limit preservation of the set inverse image. Identify object and morphism formulas with the specified tensor scalar-extension pullback. Apply the ringed-topos K-flat pullback theorem to P, retaining both the K-flat and flat-term hypotheses.
Apply the exact pullback functor mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso in each degree and reverse it. This identifies derived pullback cohomology with pullback of cohomology.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q124-33fa09041 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the full item and the statement of every cited node, the unit sk-def-sp-scalar-extension, blueprint main-20261015 sk-def-sp-scalar-extension-functor.proof.md paragraph (2), and the parent det-sp-scalar-extension-functor step that cites the item. The delivery creates no new nodes, leaves the statement unchanged and cites no SGA. A walk of the dependencies finds no cycle, and every cited id exists. Step 1: the base-change morphism and structure map c_A are the ones in def-weil-proetale-inverse-image. prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map states that c_A is invertible and equal to the def's map, including when the scheme is empty. Its coefficient sheaf Lambda_Proet is identified with the constant sheaf A_T through that prop's map, which preserves constants, so the exactness from prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact carries over; coefficients are not silently changed. Step 2: the Hom chain through the constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction (needs a final object, which exists even for an empty scheme) and the conjugate-adjoint uniqueness lemma is correct. Step 3 is genuinely elementary: naturality at the module operations, finite-product preservation, and gamma_A = c_A because both have the same adjunct. Step 4 uses Stacks 03EL (sites-modules.tex line 3649) degreewise; B_S-linearity is checked on locally constant sections, and no flatness of A->B is used. Step 5 uses Stacks 0G7E (sites-cohomology.tex line 3508), which needs both K-flatness and flat terms, exactly as the item assumes. Step 6 uses Stacks 010N with the exact functor from step 1; the finite-local-constancy hypothesis goes unused, so the item is not weakened. Edge cases checked: empty S or T, M=0, A=B, B=0, the non-flat map Z/4->Z/2, and unbounded P. Duplicate candidate: lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module (unsplit, another unit) states the general constant-module clause. The item proves that clause directly, so this is a note, not a fault.
